channel.title: Cybersecurity News
channel.description: Notable but non-breaking cybersecurity news, one finding per item: short summary plus link to the original story.

item.title: Hacktivists leak names and assignments of 41,000 DHS staff, including undercover ICE agents
item.description:
A hacktivist group calling itself the Department of Peace leaked names, offices, contact details and assignments of more than 41,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees, published by DDoSecrets on October 28 as the "Icepick" dataset. The group says the records came from an Okta single sign-on service used by DHS; Okta says it has no evidence its systems were compromised, and Reuters verified details for several named employees. CBP staff make up about 21,300 entries and ICE about 6,600, and DHS says it is aware of a potential breach.

Source: Help Net Security

item.title: CISA adds CVSS 10 GitLab RCE flaw CVE-2026-97229 to KEV with a November 1 deadline after an attack on Alpine Linux's server
item.description:
CISA added GitLab CE/EE flaw CVE-2026-97229 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 29, giving federal agencies until November 1 to fix it and requiring forensic triage. The bug in Ruby's Onigmo regex engine lets a crafted CI/CD regular expression run code on self-managed GitLab servers; it is fixed in GitLab 19.2.8, 19.3.5 and 19.4.2. Alpine Linux disclosed that an attacker tried to exploit it on its own GitLab server on October 20 and 21, and rebuilt the server, while servers that run GitLab on their own Ruby also need Ruby 3.3.13, 3.4.12 or 4.0.9.

Sources: The Hacker News, CISA KEV catalog, GitLab advisory

item.title: Linux kernel TCP flaw CVE-2026-98432 rated 9.8 by kernel team; Ubuntu and RHEL still lack fixed kernels
item.description:
CVE-2026-98432 is a use-after-free race in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP handshake code, present since Linux 4.4, which the kernel CVE team scores 9.8. Anthropic says its AI model built an exploit giving an unauthenticated remote attacker root on servers with a multipath TCP listener, though Red Hat and others score it between 5.9 and 8.1 because the race is hard to win. Debian, SUSE, Oracle Linux and Amazon Linux have shipped fixes, but Ubuntu and RHEL have no fixed kernel yet, and no in-the-wild exploitation has been reported.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: 319 Chrome extensions with 13.4 million installs caught hijacking searches for ad revenue
item.description:
Socket researcher John Tuckner found 319 Chrome extensions, with about 13.4 million combined installs, that quietly redirected users' searches through tracking servers to earn Bing and Yahoo advertising revenue. The new report adds 264 extensions and 8.7 million users to a campaign he first exposed in April 2025, and attributes them to a handful of organized operators.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Sony Network Communications breach exposes about 2.5 million customer records
item.description:
Sony Network Communications, the Sony Group subsidiary that runs an internet service provider in Japan, confirmed a breach of roughly 2.5 million records with current and former customers' personal information. The intrusion happened on October 19 and was detected four days later, when the company shut down the affected servers and blocked external communication.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Cisco patches actively exploited ASA and FTD VPN flaw CVE-2026-76418 that lets unauthenticated attackers crash firewalls
item.description:
Cisco released fixes for CVE-2026-76418 (CVSS 8.6), a flaw in Secure Firewall ASA and FTD software that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker trigger a denial of service, and says it has been exploited in the wild. Organizations running ASA or FTD VPN services should patch promptly, since a crash takes down the perimeter firewall.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Talos: attackers exploited Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN flaw to plant KeyDrift malware that steals inter-site encryption keys
item.description:
Cisco Talos said on October 28 that attackers exploited a critical Catalyst SD-WAN flaw fixed in February to plant custom malware called KeyDrift inside SD-WAN controllers. KeyDrift copies the keys that encrypt traffic between sites and stores them for later use. Talos describes the attacks as historical but did not say when they happened.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Palo Alto Networks warns PHP2Shell flaws are being exploited against internet-exposed firewall management interfaces
item.description:
Palo Alto Networks updated its advisory on October 28 to say attackers are actively exploiting the recently patched PHP2Shell vulnerabilities against management interfaces exposed to the internet. Customers should patch and restrict management access to trusted internal networks.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: CISA adds Fragnesia Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 to KEV with a three-day deadline after PHP2Shell root chain
item.description:
CISA added the Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw CVE-2026-46300, known as Fragnesia, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 28 and gave federal agencies until October 31 to fix it, with forensic triage required. CISA says attackers chain it with the PHP2Shell bugs CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to plant PHP webshells and run commands as root, the same chain Dream reported against 25 internet-facing firewall servers.

Sources: CISA KEV entry, SecurityWeek

item.title: CISA flags VMware ESX audit-logging gap CVE-2026-41709 as actively exploited
item.description:
CISA added CVE-2026-41709 in VMware ESX to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 28, with a November 11 federal deadline. The bug is rated low severity (CVSS 2.7) because it needs ESX admin access, but it lets an attacker with that access perform some operations without leaving audit-log entries, which matters for hypervisor intrusions. Broadcom fixed it in VMSA-2026-0006 for ESXi 8.0, 9.0 and 9.1 and Cloud Foundation 5.2.4; CrowdStrike reported the issue.

Sources: Broadcom advisory, CISA KEV entry

item.title: Volt Typhoon tied to "Silent Train" covert network used in four zero-day campaigns against SD-WAN and management platforms
item.description:
Lumen's Black Lotus Labs attributes a now-disrupted covert access network called Silent Train, built from rotating chains of compromised SOHO, IoT and enterprise devices, to China-linked Volt Typhoon. It was used in four confirmed zero-day campaigns: Versa Director (CVE-2024-39717), N-able N-central (CVE-2025-8875/8876), Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (CVE-2026-20127) and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (CVE-2026-16812), plus a suspected Quest KACE zero-day.

Hundreds of victims were identified across telecoms, government, defense contractors, satellite communications, universities and critical infrastructure, with the group favoring management and control-plane systems that give access to downstream customers.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: PHP2Shell used with a Linux kernel exploit to root 25 firewall servers, including a U.S. government-affiliated network
item.description:
Security firm Dream says a suspected China-nexus actor paired a custom, non-public PHP2Shell exploit with Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 on October 25 to root 25 servers running an unnamed large vendor's firewall software across the U.S., Japan, Taiwan and South Korea. Three of the servers sat in a U.S. government-affiliated environment, where the attacker moved on to Active Directory, extracting credentials and enumerating the directory. Artifacts point to AI-assisted tooling, including Claude Code and an LLM-driven offensive platform.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Oracle E-Business Suite unauthenticated SQLi-to-RCE flaw CVE-2026-101767 already drawing exploit probes days after patch
item.description:
Defused Cyber says its Oracle E-Business Suite decoys logged exploratory exploit attempts on October 27 against CVE-2026-101767 (CVSS 9.8), an unauthenticated SQL injection in the Thin Client Framework servlet that Horizon3.ai showed chains to remote code execution. Oracle fixed it in last week's Critical Patch Update.

A successful attack runs SQL as the APPS database user and OS commands as the EBS application account, exposing financial, payroll and HR data. EBS bugs have been hot targets this year, including one used by Cl0p, so internet-facing instances should be patched now.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Tailscale ships fixes for "Tailworm" SSH flaws that let one compromised device gain root on other tailnet servers
item.description:
Tailscale has released patches for several vulnerabilities, including Tailscale SSH bugs that let an attacker who already controls one device in a tailnet escalate to higher privileges on other machines. The flaws were previously reported as unpatched.

Tailscale says an attacker could only reach machines the tailnet policy file already allowed SSH connections to. Teams using Tailscale SSH should update clients and servers.

Sources: Help Net Security, The Hacker News

item.title: 16-year-old EDK II UEFI flaw CVE-2026-97631 can run code before Secure Boot on PXE network-booting machines
item.description:
TianoCore rated CVE-2026-97631 9.5 out of 10: a buffer overflow in the PXE network-boot code of EDK II, the open-source base most vendors use for UEFI firmware. An unauthenticated attacker on an adjacent network can hang the boot or, with firmware-specific work, run code before Secure Boot loads.

The attack only works while a machine is network booting. A code fix exists, but no stable EDK II release includes it yet, so most users have nothing to install today.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: 345,000 email addresses exposed in September breach of Germany's AfD party, now in Have I Been Pwned
item.description:
Have I Been Pwned added more than 345,000 unique email addresses, plus email messages, from the September 2026 breach of German political party Alternative für Deutschland. HIBP flagged it as a sensitive breach, so only verified address owners and domain admins can search it.

Source: Help Net Security

item.title: Japan's GMO warns Onamae Desktop Cloud customers to shut down PCs as attacker threatens ransomware and leaks data
item.description:
GMO Internet told customers of its Onamae Desktop Cloud VPS service to disconnect from the internet and shut down after the attacker behind an October 20 intrusion threatened to trigger ransomware planted on customer servers. The breach may have put malware on up to 26,739 customer servers, and GMO has confirmed company and customer data was published online.

The attacker demanded ¥8 billion (about $50 million), which GMO says it won't pay. MetaTrader 4 and 5 trading credentials may be exposed, so customers are being told to reset passwords and end active sessions.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: Skimmer gang hijacks Convertr's shared Plausible analytics script to steal card data across Brazilian fashion stores
item.description:
Sansec found that a Brazilian card-skimming group modified a self-hosted Plausible analytics tracker run by e-commerce platform Convertr, which loads on the checkout pages of every merchant on the platform. Convertr powers checkout for dozens of major Brazilian fashion brands handling about $370 million in sales.

Sansec suspects initial access came through CVE-2026-8467, an unauthenticated command-execution flaw in Convertr's outdated Plausible Community Edition, though that is unconfirmed. By October 26 the skimmer had been refined to target Convertr's exact payment API fields.

Source: BleepingComputer

item.title: CISA adds Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 (Node2Shell / HTTP2Shell) to KEV as exploited
item.description:
CISA added the Google Brotli decoder bug CVE-2026-111497, also called Node2Shell, HTTP2Shell or Broccoli2Shell, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 27, with a November 10 federal deadline. A crafted Brotli stream lets an unauthenticated remote attacker corrupt decoder memory, leak data, crash the process or potentially run code. It reaches Node.js, Bun, Envoy and Istio with Brotli decompression, Python Brotli, brotli4j and .NET apps; fixed versions include Brotli 1.0.10, 1.1.1 and 1.2.1 and Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1.

Sources: BleepingComputer, CISA KEV catalog, CIS advisory

item.title: CISA adds Adobe Commerce and Magento file-upload flaw CVE-2026-48356 to KEV
item.description:
CISA added Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source CVE-2026-48356, a critical unrestricted file-upload flaw (CVSS 9.6, no authentication required) that can lead to code execution or account takeover, to the KEV catalog on October 27, with a November 10 deadline. Adobe fixed it in its July 2026 APSB26-73 update, so stores still on 2.4.9, 2.4.8-p5 or older unpatched builds should update now.

Sources: Adobe APSB26-73, CISA KEV catalog

item.title: TrendAI exposes AI-driven attacks on Japan, including a CyberStrikeAI setup running 44 agents against 19 organizations
item.description:
Trend Micro's TrendAI analyzed three exposed attacker servers used against organizations in Japan, with AI playing roles from full automation to tool-building help. In the first case, the open-source CyberStrikeAI pentest framework split recon, exploitation, C2, persistence, exfiltration and reporting across 44 agents, hitting at least 19 organizations (16 in Japan) in a short October 2026 window.

The other two cases were a human-led, LLM-assisted campaign that stole GIS and email data and sought cheap inference capacity, and a long-running operator hitting Cisco, Citrix, F5, Yamaha edge devices and WebLogic servers since January. Targets also spanned Taiwan, Hong Kong, the UK, France, Italy, Qatar and Colombia.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: HPE patches 72 Aruba AOS-8 and AOS-10 flaws, including eight max-severity unauthenticated RCE and auth-bypass bugs
item.description:
HPE released fixes for 72 vulnerabilities in the AOS-8 and AOS-10 operating systems behind its Aruba wireless products, 33 of them rated critical. Eight max-severity bugs (CVE-2026-79844 through CVE-2026-79851) could let unauthenticated attackers run code remotely or gain admin access. Fixed builds are AOS 8.10.0.24, 8.13.3.1, 10.4.1.14, 10.7.2.7 and 10.8.1.2 across conductors, controllers, gateways and access points.

Source: SecurityWeek

item.title: Denver Health Medical Plan notifies 238,000 members after vendor SquareML leaked a database access key
item.description:
Denver Health Medical Plan, which administers Medicaid benefits in the Denver area, is notifying 238,083 members that their personal and health information may have been exposed. Its analytics vendor SquareML says an access key to a database holding member data was published on a public website on June 27, 2025, and was not revoked until August 18, 2026. The compromised account was read-only.

Source: SecurityWeek

item.title: DreamHost suspends File Manager and resets some email and FTP passwords over an unexplained incident
item.description:
Web host DreamHost suspended its File Manager service and reset passwords for some email and FTP/SFTP users after what it calls an issue affecting several systems, including webmail. Account owners must set new passwords for affected mailbox and FTP users and tell them to change any reused passwords elsewhere. Customers have criticized the lack of detail about whether passwords were exposed.

Source: SecurityWeek

item.title: Apple backports fix for exploited CoreGraphics flaw CVE-2026-86950 to older iPhones and iPads
item.description:
Apple released iOS 18.7.11 and iPadOS 18.7.11, extending last month's fix for CVE-2026-86950 (CVSS 8.8), an out-of-bounds write in CoreGraphics that can lead to code execution when a crafted file is processed. Apple says the flaw may have been exploited in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals. The update covers older devices such as the iPhone XS, XS Max and XR, and also fixes an Audio logic issue, CVE-2026-65339.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Microsoft fixes Authenticator for Android flaw that let permissionless apps steal work-account tokens
item.description:
Microsoft fixed CVE-2026-80097 (CVSS 8.6) in Authenticator for Android version 6.2606.4246. A malicious app with no permissions could pose as a trusted Microsoft app such as Teams and collect sign-in tokens giving full access to a victim's work email, files, and calendar. Microsoft says exploitation needs the victim to complete a sign-in step and that it has not been used in attacks; update the app.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Keystone to destroy 18,835 hardware wallets after attacker steals device-verification key
item.description:
An attacker who got into Keystone's website obtained the key its hardware wallets use to prove they are genuine, which could let counterfeit devices pass the online authenticity check. Keystone found the access on October 20, will destroy 18,835 unsold devices carrying the key, and says recovery phrases and wallet keys were not involved. Owners who received a device after October 20 should contact support before using it.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Australia's ASD breaks into Amadey malware backend, cutting off 180,000 infected computers
item.description:
The Australian Signals Directorate gained access to a criminal's Amadey malware control backend and disconnected it from about 180,000 infected computers worldwide, including some in Australia. Amadey is a malware-as-a-service loader used mainly to install further payloads such as the StealC infostealer.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: University of Copenhagen systems stay down after breach exposing data of 525,000 people
item.description:
The University of Copenhagen took Workzone, Nimbus and other administrative systems offline on Monday after activity first thought to be a new attack. It now says the activity is tied to the breach disclosed last week, which exposed personal data, including national ID numbers, of about 525,000 people.

Source: Help Net Security

item.title: University of New Mexico Health diverts patients and closes 30+ clinics over cybersecurity issue
item.description:
The University of New Mexico Health System told people not to come to its main hospital in Albuquerque, diverted patients, and canceled appointments at more than 30 clinics because of a cybersecurity issue. Details on the cause and scope haven't been released yet.

Source: SecurityWeek

item.title: Bubble says attacker stole users' third-party API keys and tokens; platform partly offline during containment
item.description:
No-code platform Bubble disclosed an active security incident on Oct 26, 2026, confirming an attacker accessed third-party tokens and credentials, such as API Connector and plugin keys, belonging to a subset of users. Bubble says the attacker now appears contained, but forensics continues and the editor, live apps, file access and some plugins remain disrupted by containment steps.

Bubble users should review activity on connected third-party accounts and be ready to rotate keys when told; official notices come only from bubble.io.

Source: Bubble status page

item.title: PHP rebuilds Windows packages for 8.2 to 8.5 to fix Brotli code-execution flaw CVE-2026-111497
item.description:
PHP has rebuilt its official Windows packages for PHP 8.2 through 8.5 (builds 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 and 8.2.35-1) to bundle Brotli 1.2.1, fixing CVE-2026-111497, the Brotli memory-corruption flaw behind the Node2Shell research. It is the second Windows update in five days, after the October 21 PHP2Shell fixes.

The flaw is reachable through the cURL extension when automatic decompression is on, which Guzzle enables by default. The PHP version number does not change, so admins should check the -1 build suffix or SHA-256 hash. No attacks are reported and the flaw is not in CISA KEV.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Genesys confirms hackers took customer contact and account data from internal CRM and LMS
item.description:
Contact-center vendor Genesys says an intruder accessed internal business systems, including its CRM and learning management system, and accessed or downloaded customer and prospect data such as names, business emails, phone numbers, job titles and account details. Genesys says the incident was fully contained on October 23 and that Genesys Cloud, Engage and Engage Cloud, plus customer data and call recordings in them, were not affected.

A new group called ScarlettGroup has claimed the attack. Customers should expect targeted phishing that references Genesys.

Sources: SecurityWeek, Genesys security update

item.title: PHP2Shell now confirmed exploited in the wild: honeypots log working shells via public PoC
item.description:
Perplexity researcher Adel Karimi reports confirmed remote code execution of the PHP2Shell flaws (CVE-2026-109618/-109619) against his honeypots, with 35 shells launched from two IP addresses on October 24 using a four-stage chain that closely matches a public proof-of-concept.

Expel's Marcus Hutchins called it the highest-quality confirmation of in-the-wild exploitation so far. Karimi cautions the honeypots used a favorable single-worker Apache mod_php setup, and no second-stage payload was seen. CISA has published a Sigma detection rule but has not yet added the flaws to KEV. Patch to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35.

Sources: SecurityWeek, BleepingComputer

item.title: Siemens, Schneider Electric, ABB and other industrial vendors confirm OT products affected by PHP2Shell
item.description:
Siemens, Schneider Electric, ABB, Rockwell Automation and Johnson Controls have published advisories on the PHP2Shell flaws, and several confirm some industrial and OT products are affected.

Schneider lists EcoStruxure Security Expert (fixed in 1.48.4.0), ProLeiT LINEoptimize and EcoStruxure Control Engineering, the last with mitigations only for now. Other vendors are still assessing exposure.

Sources: SecurityWeek

item.title: Gheist campaign uses stolen GitHub tokens to dump Actions secrets from 850+ accounts' repos
item.description:
Wiz reports an automated campaign, active since September 15, that uses stolen GitHub tokens to push ci-sync-* branches with workflows that print repository secrets into Actions logs, then downloads the logs and deletes the runs. Wiz recovered more than 13,500 planted branches from more than 850 compromised accounts, including private enterprise repositories.

GitHub's safeguard for suspicious runs blocked public-repo attempts but does not cover private repositories or GitHub Enterprise Server. Affected orgs should rotate every secret the repo could read and revoke the token that pushed the branch.

Sources: The Hacker News

item.title: Two CVSS 9.9 Wasmtime flaws let malicious WebAssembly modules escape the sandbox
item.description:
The Bytecode Alliance fixed two critical bugs in Wasmtime's Cranelift compiler (one ARM64-only, CVE-2026-115893) that let an attacker-supplied WebAssembly module escape its sandbox. Risk is highest for platforms that compile other people's modules, such as Fastly Compute.

No attacks are reported. Update to 36.0.19, 48.0.7, 49.0.4 or 50.0.0; unsupported lines, including 24.x LTS, get no fix.

Sources: The Hacker News

item.title: Fortinet ships fixes for critical AI-found FortiOS flaws, withholding details until November 10
item.description:
Fortinet released security hardening updates last week for FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator, fixing critical vulnerabilities found with AI models and validated by humans.

Details stay embargoed until November 10, 2026. CISO Carl Windsor warned that attackers can use AI to find and weaponize bugs, so admins should update now rather than wait for the disclosure.

Sources: Help Net Security

item.title: Microsoft ships out-of-band .NET updates for Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497
item.description:
Microsoft released out-of-band .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22 and 10.0.14 on October 25 to fix the Brotli decoder out-of-bounds write (CVE-2026-111497) behind the Node.js "Node2Shell" research, plus other fixes including a Blazor WebAssembly debugger RCE in .NET 10.

Apps are exposed only if they decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data; ASP.NET Core and HttpClient automatic decompression are off by default. Self-contained and NativeAOT apps must be rebuilt and redeployed.

Sources: .NET Blog, Microsoft advisory

item.title: Unpatched Tailscale SSH flaws let one compromised device reach root on other servers ("Tailworm")
item.description:
Researcher Erica Windisch of Cyberdione Labs published "Tailworm," showing that an attacker who already controls one device on a Tailscale network can use Tailscale SSH port forwarding to get root on other servers that the access rules let that device reach, with no stolen passwords or keys. The lab tests covered Tailscale 1.104.2 and headscale 0.29.5; on headscale, forwarding cannot be disabled, so every SSH grant should be treated as root on the target.

As of publication there is no Tailscale security bulletin, CVE, or fixed version. Tailscale says it is working on fixes and is not recommending everyone disable Tailscale SSH; hosted-service admins can turn off forwarding per rule.

Sources: The Hacker News, Tailworm report, Tailscale statement on Reddit

item.title: PHP2Shell: Palo Alto Networks and Trail of Bits report first confirmed compromises and post-exploit activity
item.description:
As of late Friday, Palo Alto Networks and Trail of Bits say there are now confirmed compromises and post-exploitation activity tied to PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), the unauthenticated PHP remote code execution flaws patched on October 21. Researchers say weaponizing the bugs is hard, which is why mass exploitation hasn't been seen yet, but many internet-facing PHP servers remain unpatched. Amazon has said exploitation began as early as October 17, before patches shipped.

Sources: TechCrunch, Unit 42

item.title: Eye Security pushed 2 million updates to disable abandoned Popcorn Time updater that could have fueled a botnet
item.description:
Dutch firm Eye Security found that the updater in Time4Popcorn, an abandoned Popcorn Time fork, kept calling an unregistered domain, so anyone who registered it could have pushed code to the machines still running it. The firm registered the domain itself, saw about 50 requests a second, and between November 2025 and March 2026 sent more than 2 million updates to switch the updater off. It presented the work, dubbed Operation IXIM, at Hack.lu on October 22.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: CISA adds exploited Collabora Online built-in CODE server command injection CVE-2026-110447 to KEV
item.description:
CISA added CVE-2026-110447, an unauthenticated OS command injection in the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server app for Nextcloud, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 23 with an October 26 deadline and forensic triage required. The bug in the app's proxy.php runs commands as the web server user, but only while the built-in CODE server isn't running, such as after a restart, upgrade or crash. Disabling the app isn't enough: upgrade it to 26.4.303 or later or remove it. Standalone Collabora Online servers aren't affected.

Sources: Nextcloud forum, Collabora advisory, CISA KEV

item.title: Kaspersky: APT41-linked BlackX UEFI bootkit bypasses Secure Boot on patched Windows PCs missing revocations
item.description:
Kaspersky says a new UEFI bootkit called BlackX, an updated BlackLotus, hit diplomatic organizations in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan in early 2026, and it suspects China-linked APT41. BlackX loads before Windows to undermine startup and third-party security defenses and keep long-term covert access. It works on fully patched systems where Microsoft's manual Secure Boot revocation mitigations were never applied, though attackers first need admin or physical access.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Ruby patches three Onigmo regex engine bugs behind four critical GitLab RCE flaws
item.description:
Ruby released 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 to fix three memory-corruption bugs in Onigmo, its built-in regular expression engine, which can lead to code execution when an app compiles a regex from attacker-controlled text. The bugs sit behind four critical GitLab CVEs patched between September 23 and October 21, including two from October (CVE-2026-97229 and CVE-2026-110264) that need no account. Regexp.timeout and pattern-length caps do not help, Ruby 4.0.8 misses one fix, and Ruby 3.2 and earlier get no patch. No in-the-wild exploitation has been reported.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: INC and The Gentlemen ransomware affiliates ran AI-agent intrusions against edge devices, exposed server shows
item.description:
SOCRadar found an exposed server belonging to a Russian-speaking operator serving INC and The Gentlemen ransomware affiliates, running an AI framework called Phantom that executed intrusions through OpenCode and commercial models while a human approved each step. Logs covered 8,257 messages across 133 sessions. Initial access came from exploiting edge and remote-access systems at scale, including SimpleHelp CVE-2024-57727, FortiClient EMS CVE-2026-35616 and cPanel/WHM CVE-2026-41940, followed by credential theft, lateral movement and ransomware staging.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: CISA adds exploited Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw CVE-2026-114625 to KEV with a three-day deadline
item.description:
CISA added Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator SQL injection flaw CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS 9.9) to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on October 23, with an unusually short federal deadline of October 26 and forensic triage required. Any authenticated VCO user, even with the lowest tenant role, can gain superuser operator privileges on on-prem deployments, which Arista says are exposed by default.

It is the third exploited VCO zero-day in four months. Fixed releases are 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12; Arista also lists two attacker IPs to block and hunt for in logs.

Sources: SecurityWeek, CISA KEV catalog, Arista advisory

item.title: k0t campaign breached FortiGate and GlobalProtect edge devices worldwide, exposing 70,000+ credentials
item.description:
Group-IB and NyxLab detailed a large campaign by an initial access broker tracked as k0t that indiscriminately hit exposed Fortinet FortiGate and Palo Alto GlobalProtect devices, exposing more than 70,000 credentials. Most compromises happened between February and June 2026, overlapping the FortiBleed credential-harvesting wave, and some victims saw persistent access and data theft. The actor is linked to the Qilin and The Gentlemen ransomware operations.

Source: The Hacker News

item.title: Huntress: token-spraying campaign hijacked Microsoft 365 mailboxes at 79 organizations without passwords
item.description:
Huntress tracked an attacker who, from July 14 to September 22, replayed stolen Microsoft 365 session tokens (gathered via adversary-in-the-middle phishing and device-code phishing) to break into email accounts at 79 organizations, bypassing MFA. The attacker registered at least 48 rogue devices in victims' Entra directories and used hidden inbox rules to hide mail from victims. Sign-ins came from a handful of addresses in 193.26.115.0/24 hosted by 1337 Services GmbH.

Source: Help Net Security

item.title: Critical Pillow flaw CVE-2026-112900 allows command execution via a crafted EPS filename; fixed in 13.0.0
item.description:
Pillow, Python's most widely used image library (about 436 million downloads a month), passes EPS filenames to Ghostscript unchecked, so an attacker who controls the filename can get OS commands run on hosts with Ghostscript installed. The bug, CVE-2026-112900 (rated 9.2 in the GitHub CVE record), affects versions 2.6.0 through 12.3.0 and is fixed in Pillow 13.0.0, a large security release. No exploitation is known.

Source: The Hacker News
